column6: @gap{4 lines missing} The roaring storm covered it like a cloak, was spread over it like a sheet. It covered @wSN{Eridug} like a cloak, was spread over it like a sheet. In the city, the furious storm resounded ……. In @wSN{Eridug}, the furious storm resounded ……. Its voice was smothered with silence as by a gale. Its people ……. @wSN{Eridug} was smothered with silence as by a gale. Its people …….

Its king stayed outside his city as if it were an alien city. He wept bitter tears. Father @wDN{Enki} stayed outside his city as if it were an alien city. He wept bitter tears. For the sake of his harmed city, he wept bitter tears. Its lady, like a flying bird, left her city. The mother of @wTN{E-maḫ}, holy @wDN{Damgalnuna}, left her city. The divine powers of the city of holiest divine powers were overturned. The divine powers of the rites of the greatest divine powers were altered. In @wSN{Eridug} everything was reduced to ruin, was wrought with confusion.

The evil-bearing storm went out from the city. It swept across the Land -- a storm which possessses neither kindness nor malice, does not distinguish between good and evil. @wGN{Subir} came down like rain. It struck hard. In the city where bright daylight used to shine forth, the day darkened. In @wSN{Eridug} where bright daylight used to shine forth, the day darkened. As if the sun had set below the horizon, it turned into twilight. As if @wDN{An} had cursed the city, alone he destroyed it. As if @wDN{Enlil} had frowned upon it, @wSN{Eridug}, the shrine @wTN{Abzu}, bowed low.
1st @fsux{kirugu}.
It cried out bitterly: @q[Eridug,]{“O the destruction of the city! The destruction of the house!”}
Its @fsux{ŋišgiŋal}.

A second time the storm destroyed the city -- its song was plaintive. …… was trampled. …… intensified the lament. It cut the lock from its main gate. The storm dislodged its door. …… It stacked the people up in heaps. …… on its own destroyed it. It turned …… into tears. …… defiled …… @gap{1 line missing}

…… It distorted its appearance. …… It distorted its appearance. It circled its …… wall. It overturned its foundations. Throughout his city, the pure, radiant place, the foundations were filled with dust. It cast down its ziggurat, the shrine which reaches up to heaven, into a heap of debris. The loftiness of its elevated door-ornament, befitting a house, was stripped down. It cut down the gate, its Great-Ziggurat-of-Heaven-and-Earth-Covered-with-Terrible-Awesomeness, its shining door, and it broke through its bolt. It ripped out its doorframe. The house was defaced.

Destruction ……. Throughout his house, radiant in silver and lapis lazuli, tears …….

Bitterly Father @wDN{Enki} uttered a lament for himself.
Its @fsux{ŋišgiŋal}.

Because of this, @wDN{Enki}, king of the @fsux{abzu}, stayed outside his city as if it were an alien city. It bowed its neck down to the ground. @wSN{Eridu's} lady, holy @wDN{Damgalnuna}, the faithful cow, the compassionate one, clawed at her breast, clawed at her eyes. She uttered a frenzied cry. She held a dagger and a sword in her two hands -- they clashed together.

She tore out her hair like rushes, uttering a bitter lament: @q[Damgalnuna,Eridug]{“You, my city whose woman does not dwell there, whose charms do not satisfy her -- where is a lament uttered bitterly for you? @wSN{Eridug}! You, my city whose woman does not dwell there, whose charms do not satisfy her -- where are tears wept for you? I fall like a bull in your lofty …… falls ……. I am ……. My heart …… queen …….”} @gap{unknown no. of lines missing} @notegap{incorporating end of 5th @fsux{kirugu}}

@gap{1 line fragmentary} …… far away …… the great gods. Lord @wDN{Enlil}, king of the lands, looked maliciously at @wGN{Sumer}. He demolished it. He destroyed the @wTN{Ki-ur}, the great place. He razed with the pickaxe all of the shining @wTN{E-kur}. He destroyed it but did not abandon it -- at the lunches, in his great dining hall, they call his name.

@wDN{Aruru}, the sister of @wDN{Enlil}, destroyed her city @wSN{Iri-saŋ-rig}. In @wSN{Keš}, the creation place of the Land, the people saw inside its holy sanctuary where daylight had been unknown. She destroyed it but did not abandon it -- at the lunches, in her great dining hall, they call her name. Lord @wDN{Nanna}, Lord @wDN{Ašimbabbar}, destroyed his city @wSN{Urim}. He decimated the Land with famine. He committed a sacrilege against the @wTN{E-kiš-nu-ŋal}. He struck at its heart. He destroyed it but did not abandon it -- at the lunches, in his great dining hall, they call his name.

@wDN{Inana}, the queen of heaven and earth, destroyed her city @wSN{Unug}. Fleeing from the @wTN{E-ana}, the house of seven corners and seven fires ……, she destroyed it but did not abandon it -- at the lunches, in her great dining hall, they call her name.
(@wDN{Damgalnuna} speaks:) @q[Damgalnuna,Enki]{“My beloved, who has ever seen such a destruction as that of your city @wSN{Eridug}!”}
6th @fsux{kirugu}.
@q{“My beloved, for how long was it built? For how long is it destroyed? …… adornment of the @wTN{Abzu}.”}
Its @fsux{ŋišgiŋal}.

@q[Damgalnuna,Enki]{“Lord @wDN{Enki}, who has ever seen such a destruction as that of your city @wSN{Eridug}? Who has ever seen such a misfortune as that of the shrine @wTN{Abzu}, your house?”} No one goes up to his offering terrace. At the lunches, in his great dining hall, they do not call his name. @wDN{Enki}, king of the @fsux{abzu}, felt distressed, felt anxious. At the words of his spouse, he himself began to wail. He lay down and fasted.

My king, you must not be distressed, you must not be anxious. Father @wDN{Enki}, you must not be distressed, you must not be anxious. Son of @wDN{An}, return your heart to your @wTN{Ki-ur} and your attention to your city. Living in an alien city is miserable -- return your attention to your city. Living in an alien house is miserable -- return your attention to your house. What can anyone compare with this city? -- Return your attention to your city. What can anyone compare with this house? -- Return your attention to your house. @wSN{Eridug's} day is long. Its night is over.

May your throne say to you @q[throne,Enki]{“Sit down”}. May your bed say to you @q[bed,Enki]{“Lie down”}. May your house say to you @q[house,Enki]{“Be rested”}. May your holy dais also say joyfully to you @q[dais,Enki]{“Sit down”}. May your father @wDN{An}, the king of the gods, satisfy your heart. A person, a humble man, brings you a lament over your wife's faithful house. When he sings it before you, may that person soothe your heart. When he recites a prayer, look kindly upon him.
